text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page fired: P0 -> dedicated-tenant 'equinox' latency spike (p95 > 1.8s). Link: <https://pagerduty.example/INC12345|INC12345> auto-runbook: <https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-latency>
pagerduty: Incident INC12345 created for service=dedicated-ingress, severity=P0, routed to eng-oncall.
mia: acked INC12345 and taking ownership. I'm oncall for the next 30m.
mia: quick summary: p95 latency is ~2.1s for tenant=equinox across eu-west-1; error rate is nominal (~0.2%) but client timeouts reported. Dashboards show GPU utilization on pool gpu-dedicated-7 at 96% and queue growth on reserved-queue-equinox.
sam: copying dashboards. Are we seeing KV cache evictions or long tail batch queues?
lee: checking pool metrics now — looks like an autoscaler failed to add nodes; recent control-plane errors around 1718305300 complaining about quota. Also see increased batch size for their traffic, batching window jumped to 200ms.
customer_success: equinox support pinged us ~5m ago: "Customers seeing request timeouts on inference endpoints, slow responses on search." They're seeing user-facing slowdowns.
mia: ok. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) manual scale reserved pool to add 2 GPUs, 2) temporarily reduce client-side batch window for tenant to 50ms via routing policy, 3) enable burst capacity if quota allows. I'll run commands.
lee: runbook suggests scale command: ```redwoodctl reserved scale --tenant equinox --pool gpu-dedicated-7 --delta 2``` do it when ready.
mia: running scale now. ```redwoodctl reserved scale --tenant equinox --pool gpu-dedicated-7 --delta 2 --reason "INC12345 p95 latency spike"``` deploying...
deploy-bot: scale job accepted: job_id=scale-7892, starting allocation. Watch logs: <https://infra.logs/scale-7892>
pagerduty: INC12345 acknowledged by mia at 1718305440.
sam: while scaling, let's short-circuit large batches: updating routing override to set batching.max_window_ms=50 for equinox. Command: ```redwoodctl routing set --tenant equinox --override batching.max_window_ms=50```
lee: applied routing override, confirmed at 1718305480. Backend shows batching median now down from 180ms -> 45ms.
ops_lead: heads-up on costs: if burst capacity + manual scale stays for >1h we'll hit overage. Good to resolve then revert.
customer_success: communicated to equinox: "We have identified elevated inference latency and are scaling your dedicated pool and reducing batching to mitigate. We'll update in 15m." They asked for ETA on fix.
mia: good call. I'll update in 10m. monitoring p95 in the next 2 mins.
deploy-bot: scale job scale-7892: alloc 2 GPUs provisioned at 1718305555. Pools: gpu-dedicated-7 now +2 nodes.
sam: seeing p95 drop to 1.0s now; queue depth decreasing.
mia: p95 now 0.65s, error rate steady. Looks like mitigation worked. I'll keep the override and extra nodes for 20 more minutes then start handoff.
incident-bot: auto-escalation window passed (10m) — no further escalation.
ops_lead: please ensure we open a follow-up ticket for root cause (autoscaler quota check + batching policy regression) and tag cost owner.
mia: filing followup: https://tickets.redwood/INC12345-followup created. Summary: autoscaler failed to scale due to transient control-plane quota error; batching policy for equinox regressed with a client-side change causing larger windows.
sam: taking over bridge for handoff from mia. I'll monitor for another 30m then coordinate with infra team to revert the temporary overrides if stable.
mia: handing off to sam. key actions taken: manual +2 GPU scale, batching override to 50ms, customer notified. Leaving notes in runbook and ticket.
customer_success: equinox replied: "Thanks, things are back to normal from our side." :thumbsup:
sam: marking incident as mitigated. Will keep extra capacity until 1718307232 then revert if metrics remain stable.
mia: thanks team. ops_lead can you own the postmortem and cost impact calc?
ops_lead: will take postmortem ownership. Assigning to infra and customer eng. Will include mitigation timeline and cost estimate.
sam: closing thread for now, will reopen if latency creeps up. Good job everyone. :tada:
